## Intro

10x multiome measures gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same
nuclei. This vignette takes the unsorted 3k PBMC data set (Cell Ranger ARC
2.0.0) from the raw files to linked peaks and genes: fragment QC and multiplet
calls, peaks called per cluster, TF-IDF and LSI, the weighted nearest
neighbour graph over both modalities, gene activity and label transfer,
differential accessibility and peak to gene links.

ATAC lives next to the RNA in a `SingleCellsMultiModal`: a second store under
`atac/` with peaks as features, log-CPM as the norm until `run_tfidf_sc()`
switches it to TF-IDF. Its cells are the RNA cells, in the same order, so the
RNA cell filter applies to both. Read the
[multi-modal vignette](https://gregorlueg.github.io/bixverse/articles/multi_modal_single_cells.html)
first if you have not. ATAC without RNA has
[its own vignette](https://gregorlueg.github.io/bixverse/articles/atac_only.html).

The numerics are ports, checked against the originals on test data: Signac
for the counting, QC, TF-IDF, LSI and gene activity, MACS3 for the peak
calling, AMULET for the multiplets and Seurat for the label transfer. Motif
analysis (chromVAR) and coverage tracks are not in bixverse yet.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(bixverse)
library(bixverse.plots)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
```

## The data

`download_pbmc_multiome()` fetches the filtered feature barcode matrix (RNA and
Cell Ranger's peak counts in one h5), the fragment file with its tabix index,
Cell Ranger's peaks, the GENCODE v32 annotation Cell Ranger ARC's GRCh38
reference was built from, and the ENCODE hg38 blacklist.

```{r}
#| label: paths
data_dir <- download_pbmc_multiome()
h5_path <- file.path(data_dir, "pbmc_unsorted_3k_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
fragments <- file.path(data_dir, "pbmc_unsorted_3k_atac_fragments.tsv.gz")
gtf <- file.path(data_dir, "gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz")
blacklist <- file.path(data_dir, "hg38-blacklist.v2.bed.gz")

exp_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc_multiome")
dir.create(exp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Loading

The RNA comes from the `Gene Expression` rows of the h5, the ATAC from its
`Peaks` rows. `add_atac_tenx_sc()` writes the peak store for every cell of the
RNA store, in its order; it counts Tn5 insertions, as Cell Ranger does.

```{r}
#| label: load
sc_object <- SingleCellsMultiModal(dir_data = exp_dir)
sc_object <- load_tenx_h5(sc_object, h5_path = h5_path, .verbose = FALSE)
sc_object <- add_atac_tenx_sc(sc_object, h5_path = h5_path, .verbose = FALSE)

sc_object
```

```{r}
#| label: var atac
head(get_sc_var(sc_object, modality = "atac"))
```

## Quality control

Per cell from the fragment file: fragments, nucleosome signal (mono- over
nucleosome-free fragments), TSS enrichment, the fraction on chrM and the
fraction of insertions in peaks. Cell Ranger ARC leaves chrM out of the
fragment file, so the ATAC mito fraction is zero throughout here; the RNA side
has its own.

```{r}
#| label: fragment qc
sc_object <- fragment_qc_sc(sc_object, fragments = fragments, gtf = gtf)

var <- get_sc_var(sc_object)
mito <- var[grepl("^MT-", gene_name), gene_id]
sc_object <- gene_set_proportions_sc(
  sc_object,
  gene_set_list = list(MT = mito),
  .verbose = FALSE
)
```

The two library-level checks first: insertions pile up at TSSs, and fragment
lengths come in nucleosome steps. A flat TSS profile or a smooth length
distribution means a failed library, whatever the per-cell numbers say.

```{r}
#| label: fragment profiles
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| eval: !expr utils::packageVersion("bixverse.plots") >= "0.4.0"
profiles <- fragment_profiles_sc(sc_object, fragments = fragments, gtf = gtf)

tss_profile_plot_sc(profiles$tss) + fragment_length_plot_sc(profiles$lengths)
```

```{r}
#| label: tss against fragments
obs <- sc_object[[c(
  "cell_id",
  "lib_size",
  "nnz",
  "MT",
  "atac_n_fragments",
  "atac_lib_size",
  "atac_nucleosome_signal",
  "atac_tss_enrichment",
  "atac_frip"
)]]

ggplot(obs, aes(x = atac_n_fragments, y = atac_tss_enrichment)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Fragments per cell", y = "TSS enrichment") +
  theme_bx()
```

### Multiplets

Nuclei carry two copies of each chromosome, so a locus covered by more than
two of a cell's fragments points at a second nucleus. AMULET counts those loci
per cell and tests them against a Poisson background, without clustering or
RNA. Regions that pile up fragments in every cell, the blacklist, are left
out; a repeat list would clean the calls further.

```{r}
#| label: amulet
sc_object <- amulet_sc(sc_object, fragments = fragments, restrict_beds = blacklist)

multiplet <- sc_object[["amulet_multiplet"]][[1]]
sprintf("%i of %i cells called multiplets", sum(multiplet), length(multiplet))
```

### Thresholds

On the ATAC side we keep cells with 1,000 to 100,000 insertions in peaks, a
nucleosome signal under 2 and a TSS enrichment over 2, cut-offs that sit in
the tails of the distributions above. On the RNA side we flag MAD outliers on
library size and genes, and cells above 3 MADs of mitochondrial share.

```{r}
#| label: atac thresholds
atac_qc <- run_cell_qc_fixed(
  metrics = list(
    atac_lib_size = obs$atac_lib_size,
    atac_nucleosome_signal = obs$atac_nucleosome_signal,
    atac_tss_enrichment = obs$atac_tss_enrichment
  ),
  cells_to_keep = get_cells_to_keep(sc_object),
  hard_thresholds = list(
    atac_lib_size = c(lower = 1000, upper = 100000),
    atac_nucleosome_signal = c(upper = 2),
    atac_tss_enrichment = c(lower = 2)
  )
)

plots <- violin_plot_sc(atac_qc)
plots$atac_lib_size + plots$atac_nucleosome_signal + plots$atac_tss_enrichment
```

```{r}
#| label: rna thresholds
rna_qc <- run_cell_qc(
  metrics = list(
    log10_lib_size = log10(obs$lib_size),
    log10_nnz = log10(obs$nnz),
    MT = obs$MT
  ),
  cells_to_keep = get_cells_to_keep(sc_object),
  directions = c(
    log10_lib_size = "twosided",
    log10_nnz = "twosided",
    MT = "above"
  ),
  threshold = 3
)

plots <- violin_plot_sc(rna_qc)
plots$log10_lib_size + plots$log10_nnz + plots$MT
```

```{r}
#| label: set cells to keep
drop <- atac_qc$combined | rna_qc$combined | multiplet
sprintf(
  "ATAC fails %i, RNA fails %i, multiplets %i, dropped %i of %i",
  sum(atac_qc$combined),
  sum(rna_qc$combined),
  sum(multiplet),
  sum(drop),
  length(drop)
)

sc_object <- set_cells_to_keep(sc_object, obs$cell_id[!drop])
```

## RNA

Highly variable genes, PCA, kNN, Leiden. These clusters are what the peaks get
called on below.

```{r}
#| label: rna workflow
sc_object <- find_hvg_sc(sc_object, hvg_no = 2000L, .verbose = FALSE)
sc_object <- calculate_pca_sc(sc_object, no_pcs = 50L, .verbose = FALSE)
sc_object <- find_neighbours_sc(
  sc_object,
  no_embd_to_use = 30L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
sc_object <- find_clusters_sc(sc_object, res = 0.8, .verbose = FALSE)
sc_object <- umap_sc(sc_object, no_embd_to_use = 30L, .verbose = FALSE)

embedding_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  embedding = "umap",
  colour_by = "leiden_clustering",
  discrete = TRUE,
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

## Peaks

Cell Ranger calls peaks on all cells pooled, which under-calls rare
populations. We call them per RNA cluster with bixverse's port of MACS3
`callpeak` (`--nomodel --extsize 200 --shift -100` on the Tn5 insertions),
merge the clusters' peaks, drop those on blacklist regions and on contigs, and
recount the fragments against the merged set. The new store replaces the Cell
Ranger one.

```{r}
#| label: call peaks
cr_peaks <- nrow(get_sc_var(sc_object, modality = "atac"))

peaks <- call_peaks_sc(
  sc_object,
  fragments = fragments,
  group_by = "leiden_clustering"
)
peaks <- peaks[grepl("^chr[0-9XY]+$", chrom)]
peaks <- remove_blacklisted(peaks, blacklist)
sprintf(
  "Cell Ranger peaks: %i, merged per-cluster peaks: %i",
  cr_peaks,
  nrow(peaks)
)

sc_object <- add_atac_fragments_sc(
  sc_object,
  fragments = fragments,
  peaks = peaks,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
sc_object <- annotate_peaks_sc(sc_object, gtf = gtf)

head(get_sc_var(sc_object, modality = "atac"))
```

## TF-IDF and LSI

TF-IDF over the kept cells, then a truncated SVD of the TF-IDF. We keep peaks
above the 25th percentile of total counts: the bottom quarter is mostly noise
at this depth. The first LSI component of ATAC data usually tracks
sequencing depth rather than cell identity; `calculate_lsi_sc()` leaves it out
of the embedding by default, and the depth plot shows whether that is right
here (hollow points are the components left out).

```{r}
#| label: tf-idf and lsi
sc_object <- run_tfidf_sc(sc_object)
sc_object <- find_top_features_sc(sc_object, min_cutoff = "q25")
var_atac <- get_sc_var(sc_object, modality = "atac")
sprintf(
  "%i of %i peaks kept for the LSI",
  sum(var_atac$top_feature),
  nrow(var_atac)
)

sc_object <- calculate_lsi_sc(sc_object, .verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: lsi depth correlation
#| eval: !expr utils::packageVersion("bixverse.plots") >= "0.4.0"
lsi_depth_plot_sc(get_lsi_depth_cor(sc_object))
```

```{r}
#| label: atac umap
sc_object <- find_neighbours_sc(
  sc_object,
  embd_to_use = "lsi",
  no_embd_to_use = 30L,
  modality = "atac",
  .verbose = FALSE
)
sc_object <- umap_sc(
  sc_object,
  embd_to_use = "lsi",
  modality = "atac",
  .verbose = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: atac umap plot
#| eval: !expr utils::packageVersion("bixverse.plots") >= "0.4.0"
embedding_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  embedding = "umap",
  embd_modality = "atac",
  colour_by = "leiden_clustering",
  discrete = TRUE,
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

The RNA clusters stay together on the ATAC UMAP: the two modalities come from
the same nuclei.

## Weighted nearest neighbours

WNN fuses the RNA PCA and the ATAC LSI per cell, weighting each by how well it
predicts the cell's neighbourhood.

```{r}
#| label: wnn
sc_object <- generate_wnn_graph_sc(
  sc_object,
  modality_2 = "atac",
  embd_to_use_2 = "lsi",
  no_embd_to_use_1 = 30L,
  no_embd_to_use_2 = 30L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
sc_object <- find_clusters_sc(
  sc_object,
  modality = "wnn",
  name = "wnn_clusters",
  res = 0.8,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
sc_object <- umap_sc(sc_object, modality = "wnn", .verbose = FALSE)

embedding_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  embedding = "umap",
  embd_modality = "wnn",
  colour_by = "wnn_clusters",
  discrete = TRUE,
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

```{r}
#| label: markers on wnn
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
markers <- c("CD3D", "CD8A", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A", "NKG7", "LYZ", "IL7R")
marker_ids <- var[match(markers, gene_name), gene_id]

feature_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  features = marker_ids,
  feature_labels = setNames(markers, marker_ids),
  embedding = "umap",
  embd_modality = "wnn",
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

## Gene activity and label transfer

Gene activity counts fragments over gene body plus 2 kb upstream into a gene
by cell store of its own, the shared feature space for moving labels from an
RNA reference onto ATAC cells. With paired data we know the answer: the RNA
clusters of the same nuclei. Transfer them through gene activity and the ATAC
LSI and count how many come back.

```{r}
#| label: gene activity and transfer
ga <- gene_activity_sc(
  sc_object,
  fragments = fragments,
  gtf = gtf,
  .verbose = FALSE
)

transfer <- transfer_labels_seurat_sc(
  reference = sc_object,
  query = ga,
  label_column = "leiden_clustering",
  weight_embedding = get_embedding(sc_object, "lsi", modality = "atac"),
  .verbose = FALSE
)

truth <- sc_object[["leiden_clustering", filtered = TRUE]][[1]]
sprintf(
  "transferred label equals the RNA cluster for %.1f%% of cells",
  100 * mean(transfer$predicted_leiden_clustering == as.character(truth))
)
```

Gene activity is a separate `SingleCells`, so the RNA tools run on it.
Methods built on an mRNA count model (residuals, doublet scores) refuse it,
and those that gene length biases (AUCell, ScType, NMF) warn.

The same markers as above, as gene activity instead of expression:

```{r}
#| label: gene activity of markers
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| eval: !expr utils::packageVersion("bixverse.plots") >= "0.4.0"
feature_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  features = marker_ids,
  feature_labels = setNames(markers, marker_ids),
  embedding = "umap",
  embd_modality = "wnn",
  expr_sc = ga,
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

## Differential accessibility

The marker functions take `modality = "atac"` and test peaks instead of genes,
here every WNN cluster against the rest. On ATAC the default test is a
logistic regression per peak with the library size as covariate
(`group ~ peak + depth` against `group ~ depth`), so a cluster with deeper
cells does not light up every peak. `method = "wilcox"` runs the Wilcoxon on
the TF-IDF instead.

Don't read these p-values as inference. Every cell counts as a replicate, so
with a few hundred cells per cluster they go astronomically small with either
test; use them to rank peaks. The closest gene from `annotate_peaks_sc()`
names them.

```{r}
#| label: differential accessibility
da <- find_all_markers_sc(
  sc_object,
  column_of_interest = "wnn_clusters",
  modality = "atac",
  .verbose = FALSE
)
annotation <- get_sc_var(
  sc_object,
  modality = "atac",
  cols = c("feature_id", "closest_gene", "distance_to_tss")
)
da <- merge(da, annotation, by = "feature_id", all.x = TRUE)

da[fdr < 0.05, .N, by = grp][order(grp)]
```

```{r}
#| label: top peaks
head(da[fdr < 0.05][order(-lfc)], 10)
```

A top peak's accessibility on the WNN UMAP:

```{r}
#| label: top peak plot
#| eval: !expr utils::packageVersion("bixverse.plots") >= "0.4.0"
top_peak <- da[fdr < 0.05][order(-lfc)]$feature_id[1]

feature_plot_sc(
  sc_object,
  features = top_peak,
  embedding = "umap",
  expr_modality = "atac",
  embd_modality = "wnn",
  point_size = 0.5
)
```

## Peak to gene links

A peak whose accessibility rises and falls with a nearby gene's expression
across cell states is a candidate regulatory element for that gene.
`peak_to_gene_sc()` sums both modalities over groups of cells, here fine WNN
clusters, correlates every peak within 250 kb of a TSS with the gene, and
tests the correlation. Fine clusters rather than the cells themselves: single
cells are too sparse for a correlation to mean anything.

```{r}
#| label: peak to gene
sc_object <- find_clusters_sc(
  sc_object,
  modality = "wnn",
  name = "wnn_fine",
  res = 5,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
links <- peak_to_gene_sc(
  sc_object,
  gtf = gtf,
  group_by = "wnn_fine",
  min_cells = 10L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)

sprintf(
  "%i links at FDR < 0.05 over %i genes",
  nrow(links),
  uniqueN(links$gene_id)
)
head(links[order(-r)], 10)
```
